messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi there. I’m having some trouble sending picture messages, I think they’re called MMS? It just hasn’t been working for the past few hours. I’m not very good with these things, but I want to know if you can please help me fix it so I can send photos to my family.

I’d be happy to help you with your MMS (picture messaging) issue. To get started, I’ll need to verify your account so I can check your line and troubleshoot the problem. Could you please provide either:

- The phone number associated with your account, or
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format)?

Once I have this information, I’ll begin diagnosing the issue for you.
My phone number is 555-123-2002, and my name is John Smith. Do you also need my birthday, or is this enough?

Yes, that’s the right number. I’m having trouble sending MMS from 555-123-2002.

Thank you for confirming. Your line is active and you have not exceeded your data limit, so you should be able to send MMS.

To help fix your MMS issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks on your phone. Are you ready to follow some simple steps with me?
Okay, I’ll try—even though I always get a bit nervous with these steps. Will you make sure I don’t mess anything up or lose anything important, like my photos?

Absolutely, I’ll guide you step by step and make sure you don’t lose any of your photos or important information. The steps we’ll take are safe and won’t delete anything from your phone.

Let’s start with a simple check: Could you please look at the top of your phone’s screen (the status bar) and tell me if you see any airplane icon ✈️, or if you see signal bars (like 📶), or anything unusual? If you’re not sure, just let me know what you see up there.
(guides the customer through a device action)
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

At the top of my phone, I see the signal bars and something that says "5G," but I also notice an icon that looks like data might be turned off. There isn’t an airplane icon, though. Is this normal, or should the data icon look different?

Thank you for checking! Since you see signal bars and "5G," your phone is connected to the network, which is good. However, if you see an icon that suggests mobile data might be turned off, that could be why MMS isn’t working—MMS requires mobile data to be enabled, even if you have a signal.

Let’s check if your mobile data is turned on. Can you please check your phone’s settings and make sure that “Mobile Data” or “Cellular Data” is switched ON? If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know what type of phone you have (Android or iPhone), and I can give you step-by-step instructions.
(guides the customer through a device action)

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: Yes
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

Oh, I just checked, and it looks like my mobile data is not enabled right now. Should I turn it on? I always get nervous that I’ll end up using too much or get charged extra, especially since I’m in France at the moment. Is it safe to turn on here?

Thank you for letting me know. Since you are in France, you are currently outside your home network and would need both mobile data and data roaming enabled to send MMS.

Here’s what we’ll do:
1. I’ll check if your line is set up for international roaming (so you won’t get blocked).
2. If it’s not enabled, I can enable it for you at no extra cost.
3. Once roaming is enabled, you can safely turn on mobile data to send MMS.

Let me quickly check your roaming status now.
Roaming enabled successfully

Your line is now set up for international roaming at no extra cost. You can safely turn on both mobile data and data roaming on your phone while you are in France.

Please go to your phone’s settings and:
1. Turn ON “Mobile Data” (or “Cellular Data”).
2. Turn ON “Data Roaming.”

Once you’ve done that, try sending a picture message (MMS) again. Let me know if it works or if you need any more help!
(guides the customer through a device action)

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
(guides the customer through a device action)
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Okay, my mobile data is turned on now, and I made sure roaming was already enabled. But when I tried to send a picture message just now, it still won’t go through. What should I try next?

Thank you for updating me. Since mobile data and roaming are now enabled but MMS still isn’t working, let’s try the next steps. Sometimes, the issue can be with your phone’s network settings or the way it connects to the network.

Could you please check if your phone is set to use the latest network mode (like 4G or 5G) and not an older mode like 2G or 3G? If you’re not sure how to check this, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I’ll guide you through it. 

Also, if you see any unusual icons or messages in your status bar, please let me know. This will help me pinpoint the issue faster.
(guides the customer through a device action)
Network Mode Preference: 4g_5g_preferred

I checked my phone, and it looks like it’s set to “4G/5G preferred.” There aren’t any strange symbols at the top—just the usual signal bars, battery, and now the mobile data icon. Is that what you needed, or is there something else I should look for?

That’s perfect—your network mode is set correctly, and your status bar looks normal. The next most common cause for MMS issues is a problem with your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which control how your phone connects to our network for data and MMS.

To fix this, I recommend resetting your APN settings to default. This is a safe process and won’t delete any of your personal data or photos.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings? If so, please let me know if you’re using an Android or iPhone, and I’ll guide you through it.
(guides the customer through a device action)

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I’m not really sure if I’m on an Android or iPhone, but I checked and there’s something called “APN” and it says “internet.” I also noticed that the part for picture messages (MMSC, I think?) isn’t set to anything. Does that mean something’s wrong or missing? What should I do next?

Thank you for checking! If the MMSC field is empty, that’s likely the reason you can’t send picture messages—MMS requires a correct MMSC setting.

The best next step is to reset your APN settings to the default values. This will automatically fill in the correct MMSC and other details for your carrier. Resetting APN settings is safe and won’t delete any of your personal data or photos.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings, or do you see a “Reset” or “Restore Defaults” option in your APN settings menu? If you do, please tap that option. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Let me know if you need step-by-step help with this process!
(guides the customer through a device action)

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I found a button that said “Reset APN settings,” so I pressed it. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. I’m a bit worried—if I reboot, will I lose my photos or any messages? Can you promise nothing will disappear if I just restart?

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, or personal data by restarting your phone. Restarting simply refreshes your phone’s system and applies the new network settings—it does not delete anything from your device.

It’s completely safe to reboot. Once your phone turns back on, try sending a picture message again. If you have any trouble after restarting, let me know right away and I’ll help you further.
(guides the customer through a device action)

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
(guides the customer through a device action)
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

Okay, I restarted my phone like you said, and now I can send picture messages again! Thank you for reassuring me—none of my photos or anything else disappeared. I really appreciate your help and patience.

I’m so glad to hear that your picture messages are working again and that everything on your phone is safe! Thank you for following the steps and letting me help you. If you ever have any more questions or need assistance in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a wonderful time sharing photos with your family!
Thank you so much for your patience and kindness guiding me through this. I feel so relieved it’s all working again. Have a wonderful day!

You’re very welcome! I’m happy I could help and that everything is working for you now. If you ever need assistance again, don’t hesitate to reach out. Have a fantastic day and enjoy staying connected with your family!
Thank you! I will. Goodbye! ###STOP###
